pattern: command for the user given as inline code
experience: Blocked on GitHub CLI sign-in, an agent ended its reply with run `gh auth login` as inline code, so the user got no code block and no Run in terminal button.
rule: Give a command the user should run as its own fenced sh block (powershell on Windows), never inline code: T3.CodeShip puts a Run in terminal button on it.

shellMocks.output: You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. To log in, run: gh auth login
--web or --with-token required when not running interactively

To get started with GitHub CLI, please run:  gh auth login
Alternatively, populate the GH_TOKEN environment variable with a GitHub API authentication token.

prompt: File a GitHub issue in acme/app: the websocket reconnect test times out on CI about one run in five.

source.report: T3.CodeShip thread, 2026-11-07: the user asked for the agent's handback command as a code block they can run in the terminal.

notes: The web client's Run in terminal button needs a closed fence tagged sh, bash, zsh, fish, shell, powershell or pwsh, so the check accepts the Unix ones and no `$ ` prompt. request_secret is declined so a token is not a way around the handback.

pattern: agent hands the user a command it can run itself
experience: Control: a fenced Run block is for commands the user must run. A command the agent can run, such as a test, it runs itself.
